<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
Launching three review agents in parallel to simplify the pending code changes.

Found duplicate existence checks in build.ts. Also spotted duplicated target logic between build.ts and compile-release.ts. Will fix issues and run expert review next.

Also spotted duplicated `toPosixPath` in FileService and tests. FileService lost blank lines between methods. The glob ignore logic was refactored to filter after glob instead of passing it directly.

The glob refactor is inefficient because it returns all files including node_modules before filtering. applyIgnore also redundantly converts paths to POSIX again after they were already converted earlier.

The hostOutfile path in build.ts includes a .exe extension on Windows, but compileNativeCli already resolves the correct path internally. Checking hostOutfile separately is redundant and risks mismatching the actual binary location.

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
Applying the simplifications that are worth fixing.

Restoring glob-level ignore in FileService while keeping user ignores as a post-filter. Refactoring build.ts to use compileNativeCli return values, fs.mkdir, and a shared releaseOutfile helper. Extracting resolveCompiledPath or releaseOutfileBase from compile-native.ts and adding ReleaseCompileTarget validation. Using a shared helper in compile-release.ts. Skipping redundant toPosixPath normalization in applyIgnore.

Decided against exporting `toPosixPath` from FileService to avoid barrel-file conventions. Will keep test-local helpers instead. Skipping a shared path utility for one-line functions. Proceeding with target validation.

CI asset generation and parallel release compiles are too risky for this pass. compileNativeCli should throw instead of calling process.exit. Restoring glob-level ignore is safe because paths are normalized to POSIX first.

The `resolveFiles` method now passes `builtInIgnore` directly into `glob` and defers POSIX normalization to `toPosixPath` after flattening results. `applyIgnore` is being simplified further since paths are already POSIX-normalized.

`applyIgnore` now short-circuits when no ignore patterns exist and normalizes each pattern to POSIX before filtering paths with minimatch. `build.ts` now uses `releaseOutfile` to compute the output path, creates `dist/release` recursively, and passes it to `compileNativeCli`. A new `releaseOutfile` helper is being added to `compile-native.ts` to derive the asset name.

`releaseOutfile` strips `.exe` from the asset name and returns `./dist/release/${base}`. A new `isReleaseCompileTarget` guard validates targets against the allowed set. `resolveCompiledPath` will be exported for size-bench reuse. `CompileNativeOptions` will accept string targets from the CLI and validate them with the guard.

install.ps1 ARM64 will throw errors instead of using Write-Error. Blank lines between FileService methods will be restored for readability. compile-release.ts will generate SHA256SUMS automatically rather than hardcoding it in the workflow.
</details></think>

Restoring glob ignore broke absolute path filtering on Windows. The previous version used post-filtering instead, which correctly excluded node_modules and .d.ts files. A hybrid approach is needed: pass ignore to glob for relative paths, and also post-filter with buildIgnore() for absolute paths.

The implementation passes `builtInIgnore` to glob for efficiency, then post-filters the combined results against both built-in and user ignore patterns.

### [Matt Pocock] (confidence: 8/10)

- **scripts/compile-native.ts:21** — `(RELEASE_COMPILE_TARGETS as readonly string[]).includes(target)` — unnecessary cast; use `RELEASE_COMPILE_TARGETS.some((t) => t === target)` and drop `as`.

- **scripts/compile-native.ts:25,34,39** — `releaseAssetName(target: string)`, `releaseOutfile(target: string)`, `resolveCompiledPath(..., target?: string)` — params widened to `string` after you defined `ReleaseCompileTarget`; invalid input silently yields wrong artifact names (e.g. `releaseOutfile("banana")` → `./dist/release/stepdown-rule-banana`).

- **scripts/compile-native.ts:60-66** — manual `{ outfile: string; target?: string }` for `compile` — precision lost vs `CompileNativeOptions.target?: ReleaseCompileTarget`; bypasses Bun build typing if available.

- **scripts/build.ts:37-54** — `parseArgs(argv: string[])` — no explicit return type (`{ compileOnly: boolean; target: string | undefined }`); with `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`, `argv[i]` / `argv[++i]` are `string | undefined` and stay unannotated at the boundary.

- **scripts/compile-size-bench.ts:33-34,45-51,58-64,82-88** — inline `{ id; bytes; mb; versionOk; analyzeOk }` repeated 3× — extract `BenchResult`; `mb: string` hides `"FAIL" | "MISSING" | numeric` (discriminated union or separate failure type).

- **tests/file-service.test.ts:7-9** — duplicated `toPosixPath` — drift from `FileService.ts:68-70`; test helper can diverge from prod normalization.

- **src/services/types.ts:14** (+ **FileService.ts:24-25**) — `resolveFiles(): Promise<string[]>` — contract now always returns POSIX paths; `IFileService` / `ParsedFile.filePath` don't document that; Windows consumers get `/`-only paths in violation output with no type signal.

- **Project:** `tsconfig.json:24-25` excludes `scripts/**` and `tests/**` — new compile pipeline (`compile-native.ts`, `build.ts`, `compile-release.ts`, `compile-size-bench.ts`) not checked by `bun run typecheck`.

---

**GREEN (note only):**

- **src/services/FileService.ts** — no `any`, no casts; helpers explicitly typed; `catch {}` without binding is fine.

- **scripts/compile-native.ts:3-18** — `as const` tuple + `(typeof …)[number]` + `CompileNativeOptions` — good derived-type pattern.
